items.text: Ensure that the changes adhere to Don't Repeat Yourself (DRY) principles.
Ensure that the changes adhere to SOLID design principles.
Ensure that the changes implement functionality in the least amount of code possible.
Ensure that the change implements the stated intent and nothing else.
Ensure that boundary conditions are handled (null/None, empty, zero, negative, max values, off-by-one, etc.).
Ensure that concurrent/async paths are free of race conditions and ordering bugs.
Ensure that types, interfaces, and contracts still hold after the change.
Ensure that dead or unreachable code paths are not introduced.
Ensure that existing project patterns and layering is followed.
Ensure that naming is clear and consistent.
Ensure that function and method names are verbs; classes, types, and variables are nouns.
Ensure that no instances of premature abstractions or speculative generality were added.
Ensure that no instances of leaky or misplaced responsibility were added.
Ensure that comments explain why, not what.
Ensure that public API and breaking changes are intentional and documented.
Ensure that filenames pertain to the domain or behavior and are not generic names like `models`, `types`, `schemas`, `entities`, etc.
Ensure that errors are handled specifically, not swallowed by bare catch/except.
Ensure that failures propagate or are recovered with clear semantics.
Ensure that timeouts, retries, and cancellation are considered where I/O occurs.
Ensure that resource cleanup (files, connections, locks) happens on all paths.
Ensure that there are no obvious N+1 queries or repeated work in loops.
Ensure that hot paths avoid unnecessary allocation or quadratic algorithms.
Ensure that large payloads or unbounded collections are guarded.
Ensure that caching or batching is used only when justified and correct.
Ensure that secrets, keys, tokens, credentials, etc. are not hardcoded.
Ensure that user or external input is validated/sanitized at trust boundaries.
Ensure that queries and commands use parameterization or safe APIs (no string concatenation).
Ensure that authorization checks exist beyond mere authentication (IDOR, ownership, role).
Ensure that sensitive data is not logged, returned in errors, or exposed in responses.
Ensure that crypto uses modern primitives and correct modes; no weak hashes or ECB.
Ensure that path handling prevents traversal; redirects and URLs are validated.
Ensure that new behavior has corresponding tests (or a clear reason why not).
Ensure that tests assert real behavior, not just mock interactions.
Ensure that edge cases and failure modes are covered.
Ensure that tests fail if the production change is removed.
